thermonuclear: Both run at 294358fc: deep-review CHANGES (6 findings), code-quality CHANGES (10 findings). Each judged below; the ones not carried are listed under notCarried with the reason.

keyFindings.description: putRecord answers a non-conflict write failure exactly as a lost compare-and-set, so writeRecord returns (0, false, nil): the claim path reports ClaimedElsewhere with the sweep still Complete, the cursor moves past the record's entry, the claim's new entry is later deleted as a stray, and an unlisted open delivery is never asked for again. backfillIndex likewise counts such a record indexed and sets the marker. Before the index, the whole-bucket read re-decided it next sweep, so this is a regression of the one loss the design guards against.

A record an older build rewrites loses Pending (base's record struct has no such field). openDue then deletes its entry as a stray, the marker keeps backfillIndex from running for up to 72h, and decide's upgrade write reaches only listed deliveries, so a refusal-only delivery outside the listing is lost during a rolling deploy and after a rollback then roll-forward within 72h. The comment at 712-715 says neither needs a rule.
errPendingNotWritten after a request was made drops a Redelivered/RequestRefused/Expired decision from the report; the comment's reason is false on that path.
The stray repair can delete an entry another sweeper (an operator run, which takes no lease) has just Put and is about to name in its record write.

failed() records on context.WithoutCancel(parent); parent is the flight's base context, so the wrapper drops the owner cancellation Close relies on and Close can wait without bound on a database that stopped answering. parent itself has no sync deadline.
SyncProject's ctx.Err() break duplicates Sync's own first check and makes the doc's 'attempting each … answers each source's outcome' false.
Dead code: attention's NextAttemptAt.IsZero branch (pendingFor's clamp already gives now), parsePendingKey's unused at, and openDue's seen map, which its own comment says never fires.

sweep.go grows to 1197 lines and importer.go to 1056 while index.go exists for the index: move the index code (openDue, backfillIndex, writeRecord, dropPending, indexMarked, errPendingNotWritten) into index.go and the flight code into its own file.
Prose: 'waiting' in the running sweep is not only a listed delivery; an entry keyed to the sweep's own minute that is due later in that minute is decided Waiting too (same wording in sweep.go:34-35).
Prose: comments that narrate the change rather than the code (index.go:10-11, 22-23; sweep.go:589-590; sweep_test.go:1329; importer_test.go:718-719).
Prose: three block labels carry wrong pattern counts: *bun_install 16 over a block of 15, *legion_command 57 over 59, *dispatch_server 42 over 50. Convention: the label counts the block below it.

notCarried: Deep 5 (the starter's Idempotency-Key commit hook rides into the flight): not a defect. markRequestKeyCommitted acts only while the starter's handler runs (request_keys.go:1077), a takeover needs the holder's lease to lapse, which it does not while the handler runs, and a joined caller's unmarked key re-runs an idempotent sync.

Quality 2 (syncCount copies api/server.go backgroundWork): the two differ (refuse after close), the copy is ~40 lines and says so, and sharing it means a new package plus an edit of api/server.go outside this change; not required.
Quality 3 (writeRecord mutates Pending through its pointer): the simplify pass chose this shape and each caller that patches Pending says why; not a defect.
Quality 6 (two drain styles): style, not a defect.
Quality 9 (joinInBackground sleeps 500 ms): a joining caller makes no observable call, the helper says so, and the tester's mutation of the freshness loop turned the test red; not a defect.
